conventions.convention: Degree uses integral relative homology, the standard orientation of the Euclidean domain, and the positive local generator at the target. Empty preimage uses the zero source class.
The partial projection is h¹(μ)=αμ−βμ, where αμ and βμ integrate positive and negative parameter weights before cancellation. They need not be the Jordan parts of h¹(μ).
Signed narrow convergence means convergence against every bounded continuous real function on Θ, including when Θ is unbounded; compactly supported tests alone do not suffice.
The two-homogeneous projection is a finite nonnegative measure on the sphere weighted by squared radius. Parameter mass at zero contributes zero.
Global optimality is over finite nonnegative measures, without fixing their mass; Wasserstein flows themselves are curves of probability measures.
The relaxed partial objective uses the Jordan total-variation penalty. It equals the infimum over lifts with an integrable absolute weight, and a Jordan-sign lift attains that infimum.

Separation means every continuous path joining the specified faces or spheres intersects the support. The preservation arguments use forward characteristics and degree, without assuming a backward inverse.

AC is explicitly assumed for signed-convergence and flow arguments, supplying the inherited DC and countable-choice premises. The elementary degree, projection and convexity identities retain their stated choice-free branches.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For finite signed Borel measures σn converging against every bounded continuous real test to ν on a nonempty closed Euclidean subset, their variations have uniformly bounded masses and are uniformly tight; bounded norm-continuous separable-Hilbert-valued moments converge in norm, and the bounded-Lipschitz distance tends to zero. The stated positive-part and weighted-variation lower-semicontinuity inequalities also hold.

Under its AC and full partial feature-flow hypotheses, every flow in the definition satisfies the all-endpoint energy identity and S(t)−S(s)=−2∫sᵗ(⟨fq,mq⟩+Pq)dq. Total squared action is finite; uniformly bounded feature moments imply S(t)≤S(0)+2(DM+E0)t. No bounded-support assumption on initial weights is required.

Under the stated bounded-domain or compactified unbounded-domain hypotheses, a negative level has larger negative inner and outer thresholds and a forcing neighborhood that trap favorable angular paths. The opposite-sign equation has the corresponding backward trap, with constants independent of the interval, positive continuous speed factor and ordering of forcing values.
If bounded C¹ W≥0 gives a globally semiconvex potential |w|W(θ), then W is constant when Θ is all Euclidean space, or when Θ is the stated bounded convex domain closure with the Neumann condition.
For a finite-energy finite nonnegative measure μ and differentiable convex R, μ minimizes F over all finite nonnegative Borel measures if and only if Gμ≥0 everywhere and Gμ=0 μ-almost everywhere.

The relative-homology integer D(f,U,y) is well-defined for bounded open U, continuous f on its closure and y outside f(∂U); it has the stated normalization, preimage necessity, additivity and moving-target homotopy invariance.
Under the full stated partial-model hypotheses and signed narrow convergence h¹(μt)→ν, G+=0 ν⁺-almost everywhere and G−=0 ν⁻-almost everywhere.
Under the full partial stationarity hypotheses and signed narrow projection convergence, the actual lifted penalties converge to ∫Ṽd|ν| and F(μt)→J(ν). No initial-support separation is required.

Continuous positive two-homogeneous feature and penalty integrals factor through h²; weak convergence of the finite spherical projections gives norm convergence of feature moments and convergence of energies. Partial signed projections determine feature moments but do not alone determine lifted penalties.
Assume AC. W2 convergence implies weak convergence of h² on the sphere; on a closed Euclidean Θ, it also implies convergence of h¹ against every bounded continuous real test on Θ.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 introduces ζ as an already projected measure on the sphere but writes the moment and C¹ estimates using ‖h²(ζ)−ν‖BL. The intended quantity is ‖ζ−ν‖BL. Alternatively, explicitly viewing ζ as a measure on Rᵈ supported on the unit sphere makes h²(ζ)=ζ. As written this switches domains without stating that identification; the estimate itself closes immediately.

Fact F4 supplies particle energy monotonicity only through the external citation 'Chizat--Bach Proposition 2.3'. The declared local supplier thm-finite-particle-flows-converge-in-w2 already proves exactly the needed energy identity in Proof 3.1. Cite that local derivation explicitly so the argument's local support is visible; no new mathematical lemma is needed.
